releases.title: Hold to command
releases.summary: Your chosen villagers build, houses shelter twice as many, and a held finger draws boxes, rallies and attack-moves.
changes: The villagers you select build what you place, all of them, whatever they were doing. With none selected, the nearest free villager still goes.
Houses add 20 housing instead of 10, so fewer houses reach the 100 limit. Houses already standing in saved games keep their housing.
Hold empty ground until the ring appears, then drag to box-select your units.
Hold a production building and drag to the ground to set its rally point.
Hold a spot with soldiers selected and pull your finger down to attack-move there.
Holding and lifting in place still queues a waypoint, now when you lift rather than while your finger is down. Update before playing online.

releases.title: Openings and gold
releases.summary: Choose early pressure, a second town or a faster Castle age.
changes: Extra Town Centers unlock in Feudal for 400 wood and 100 gold. Expansion competes with your army and Castle savings.
Archers cost 50 food, 70 wood and 20 gold; Horsemen cost 180 food, 20 wood and 40 gold. Warriors remain gold-free. Gathering rates and civilization bonuses are unchanged.
Opponents vary their openings, use their civilization and visible counters when recruiting, and prepare trade as safe mines run low.
New Standard battles require five guarded minutes at Sacred. Control race and the victory timers in existing saves are unchanged.
Saved production queues retain the exact resources already paid, including refunds for older recruits. Update before playing online.

releases.title: Working trade roads
releases.summary: Opponents plan a renewable gold economy for longer battles.
changes: Opponents stop over-mining gold once upcoming purchases are covered and put those workers back on food and timber.
Castle-age armies reserve resources for a siege engine instead of endlessly spending the budget on basic troops.
When nearby safe gold runs low, opponents can save for a Trade Post and its first Trader. They avoid visibly threatened routes and expand only after a caravan proves its income.
Gathering rates, movement, map reserves and victory timers are unchanged. Existing solo saves remain compatible.

releases.title: Even stock on every seed
releases.summary: A rare diagonal-resource layout now receives its full, fair stock.
changes: Fixed a rare Twin Lakes seed that left two wood unallocated on the map's diagonal. Every resource stays mirrored and every map keeps its full finite budget.
The six-minute Standard hold, gathering rates and tested pacing maps are unchanged. Existing solo saves keep their captured world and timer.
Both online players must update to use the corrected map allocation.

releases.title: Time to counter, reasons to expand
releases.summary: Longer Standard objective battles and a clearer transition to farms and trade.
changes: New Standard matches require six guarded minutes at Sacred. Control race keeps its three-minute bank, and destroying the enemy Town Center can still win immediately.
Every map style has the same finite stock: 4,000 food, 10,000 wood and 4,000 gold. Opening berries and the stocked timber groves remain useful; distant reserves run out sooner.
Gathering rates, movement, unit costs and trade income are unchanged. Farms sustain food and protected trader routes provide renewable gold.
Existing solo saves keep their original resource amounts and victory timer. Both online players must update for the new match rules.

releases.title: Keep your caravans moving
releases.summary: Find traders quickly, see route problems, and return safely after a battle.
changes: Economy gains a compact trader finder when you have a Trade Post. Tap the cart to find your traders; stopped or blocked routes get attention first.
Trader details distinguish blocked roads, missing buildings, paused orders and working routes. Trade Posts show only controls their traders use.
Opponents at the normal population limit now send a worker to look for wood when nearby visible forests run out, instead of leaving their economy stuck on food.
Solo checkpoints now safely discard defeated targets that were still referenced during combat. Existing saves, gathering rates, trade payouts and online speed remain compatible.

releases.title: Traders take the road
releases.summary: Trade Posts can now recruit Traders, including posts in existing solo saves.
changes: Fixed a missing production queue that made the Trader button do nothing. Existing saved Trade Posts gain their working queue when resumed.
Trade placement still previews potential gold and warns about sites too near town. Routes, costs, gathering and combat balance are unchanged.

releases.title: Plan your trade road
releases.summary: See a Trade Post's potential before spending wood.
changes: Trade Post previews warn when they are too near town and show potential gold per completed trip farther away. A clear road is still required; traders confirm the actual route.
Trade guidance fits in the existing placement strip. Building Info explains when gold arrives and why the road needs protection.
Existing solo saves remain compatible. Movement, gathering rates, production costs, and online speed are unchanged.

releases.title: Save your kingdom
releases.summary: Return to your solo battle, rally your recruits, and keep more of the battlefield in view.
changes: Solo battles autosave on this device. Pause and choose Save & Exit, then Resume solo from the main menu—even after closing the app.
Saves keep the battlefield, workers and cargo, paid production, construction, armies, trade routes, explored map, and opponent progress. Failed writes preserve the previous good save.
Select a production building and tap its flag, then choose a destination. Town Centers can rally new Villagers straight to a resource, even when another worker stands over it.
A compact icon dock replaces the lower text panels. Collapse it with the chevron; tap a portrait for details. Economy, Army, and building choices use small expandable icon panels.
Five illustrated map-style cards show each landscape's character. Every new match still generates a fresh battlefield.

releases.title: New roads, clearer orders
releases.summary: Fresh battlefields, exposed trade routes, and a quieter mobile interface.
changes: Five seeded map styles, including Golden Basin and Twin Lakes, vary routes and resource positions while keeping symmetric starts.

Three starting villagers share the same civilization gathering rules as recruits. Gathering is modestly slower; farms sustain food and Traders deliver renewable gold along vulnerable Town Center–Trade Post routes.
Hold a unit card to add a finite paid queue; release or drag away to stop. Queue options and detailed management controls expand when needed.
Compact age and church controls, local placement previews, clearer movement routes, and responsive movement. Online matches always run at 1× speed.
Explored resources and buildings remain dimly visible as last seen. Hidden units and activity stay unseen until you scout again.
Updates and Refresh are available from the menu; active matches defer app updates.

releases.title: Back to work
releases.summary: A chosen delivery should not leave your worker idle.
changes: Workers return to their active gathering job after the last queued depot delivery. Later waypoints and fresh Move or Stop orders take priority.
The touch guide now explains queued routes, building rally stops, single-worker Undo and the current queue cancellation controls. Worker Info explains delivery and return behavior.
Includes the beta.10 kingdom redesign, recorded sound palette, reduced-unit economy and steadier commands. Online requires matching protocol-8 clients and server.

releases.title: Small kingdoms, deliberate commands
releases.summary: Fewer pieces to manage, steadier touch controls and a more welcoming kingdom.
changes: A shared heraldic wordmark, illustrated village medallion and gold action plaques welcome you on the web and in the game.

Workers carry and produce twice as much. Workers and ordinary soldiers now use two population, cost twice as much and take twice as long to recruit. Two starting workers preserve the opening workforce budget; ordinary soldiers have twice the health, damage and armor. The 100-population ceiling and Sacred victory clock remain.

Tap a destination repeatedly without losing selection. Hold ground to add a waypoint, or hold a friendly depot to queue a delivery. Production buildings pass their ordered rally destinations to new units. Stop or a new direct order replaces a unit route; Clear queued destinations removes pending waypoints.
Fighters temporarily defend themselves when a unit attacks them during a building assault, then return to that building if it remains valid. Explicit new player orders take priority.
Recruitment buttons keep their positions when queues change. Compact progress, waiting counts and explicit cancel controls make production easier to read on small landscape screens.

Sound effects by Kenney (kenney.nl), CC0, edited for Pocket Kingdoms: 46 recorded variants replace synthesized cues, with quiet work accents, soft fades, variation and bounded overlap. Licenses and source provenance are preserved in the repository.
Online protocol 8 requires a matching updated server and clients for the new economy and queued commands.

releases.title: Steadier hands, richer groves
releases.summary: More reliable startup, easier orders and clearer room to build.
changes: Sound modules now load through the current page's verified game cache before the engine starts, avoiding a separate module download that could fail in Safari's installed app. Genuine errors still keep their recovery controls.
Play solo and Play online have new pennant and paired-kingdom icons. What's new and Full screen share a rounded forest toolbar aligned with Settings, including smaller screens.
Battlefield choices now expand from one selected-map card. Camera and navigation tools above the minimap open from one compact View button.

After moving or reassigning a group of villagers, a temporary Undo restores their previous work or movement orders for ten seconds. It keeps current cargo and progress; unavailable old jobs stop safely. A newer worker order replaces that opportunity.
Panning retires stale double taps, and a moving unit keeps the tap that began on it. Visible silhouettes remain selectable when another unit is already selected.
New movement orders skip an unnecessary step back to the current tile center when the next segment is clear. Obstacle checks, speed and combat timing remain unchanged.

Opening berry groves and both side expansion groves contain 12 bushes instead of 8: 2,400 food per grove, adding 2,400 food per player across those guaranteed sites. Gathering rates and unit costs remain unchanged.
Building previews stay readable over trees. A solid outline shows the footprint, with distinct markings for blocked ground and the access space needed beside other buildings.
Both online players must reload for the updated maps. Saved sound and control preferences and cached Solo remain available.

releases.title: Room to command
releases.summary: Faster crowded battles, a consistent illustrated interface and Solo ready to travel offline.
changes: Large armies share precise nearby-unit and vision lookups instead of repeating full-army scans. Movement, attack timing, ownership and fog rules retain their existing behavior.
Forest cloth, warm paper and honey accents now carry through Settings, pause, results, guides, construction and management screens. Familiar icons keep their tappable explanations.

Choose your kingdom, then your battlefield, difficulty and rules. A separate More options sheet keeps population, seed and opening tips available; the launch summary keeps the chosen settings visible.

After one complete download, Solo can launch from the browser cache without a connection. The welcome screen confirms when it is saved for offline play. Updates verify and reuse unchanged files; a changed game pack still downloads as a complete file. Online battles need a connection.
Scouts now see 10 tiles instead of 8 in every civilization, with the same speed, cost and unarmed role. Both players still start with a Scout and four villagers.
Both online players must reload for the extended Scout sight. Existing modes, population choices, unit costs and action timing remain available.

releases.title: Keep your kingdom moving
releases.summary: Distinct danger cues, faster control updates and better commitment from larger AI armies.
changes: An original two-pulse wood-and-reed warning distinguishes danger from successful orders. Frequent sounds stay soft, with existing volume controls, priorities and repetition limits.
Battlefield controls avoid repeating unchanged icon decoration when switching selections, reducing interface work while preserving familiar shapes, labels, costs and shortcuts.

In larger matches, Medium and Hard opponents commit a proportionate army to a contested Sacred Site. They can use surplus troops for their existing field attacks and recall fighters when an enemy victory is close. Home defense still takes priority.
The 100-population default, starting Scouts, visible silhouettes behind scenery and tappable icon guide remain. Unit costs, stats, action timing, map layouts and online protocol are unchanged.

releases.title: Small sounds, clearer choices
releases.summary: Warm tactile sounds, clearer controls and room for hundred-population kingdoms.
changes: Soft original wood taps, cloth brushes and felt-like musical accents respond to selection, orders, work and battle. Variations, shared cooldowns and priority limits keep busy scenes restrained. Volume and mute preferences remain available in Settings.

Play solo and Play online lead to a clearer setup. Paper map cards explain each battlefield, civilization comparisons show their strengths and tradeoffs, and More options keeps population and map seed close at hand.

Softer command shelves, round utility icons and visible recruitment progress give the battlefield more room. Tap the icons in Settings > Guide or the match guide to learn what they do. Unit names, costs, availability and existing shortcuts remain available.

Units in your current vision remain readable when buildings, trees or other troops overlap them. Tap the visible silhouette to select the unit behind the obstruction. Fog still conceals unseen enemies. Town Centers use a close selection outline without the large range circle.
Both players now start with one Scout in every civilization and game mode, alongside four villagers. The opening guide recognizes the starting Scout.
Normal games now allow 100 population per player; 20, 30, 40 and 60 remain available. Houses show how much capacity they can still add and explain the match limit.
Existing unit costs, stats, gathering rates, action timing and maps are preserved. Both online players must reload for the new population settings.

releases.title: A gentler little world
releases.summary: English, French and Mongol villages, painted to belong in the landscape.
changes: All eighteen units and thirty buildings now use soft illustrated shapes, quiet colors and clear silhouettes. English timber and thatch, French limestone and slate, and Mongol felt gers each bring their own everyday details.
New crests and a painted village welcome you to the game. Portraits, recruitment cards, building cards and construction previews share the same civilization artwork.

Workers keep their feet planted as they chop, hoe and build; tools follow their hands. Infantry, bowmen, riders and siege engines have gentler windup and recovery poses, with reduced-motion options preserved.
Existing civilization bonuses, costs, health, damage, movement, collision, gathering speed, combat timing, maps and victory rules are unchanged.

releases.title: Room to settle
releases.summary: More room for your village, richer gathering grounds and settlements with a story.
changes: Choose your settlement once in New Game. Solo opponents are selected automatically; multiplayer keeps each player in control of their own choice. Rapid reopening and stale lobby confirmations are fixed.

The battlefields now have larger home clearings, richer nearby groves, wider routes and stocked expansion sites with space to build. Bases move inward without shortening the direct journey between opponents.

Meet Bellwick, Alderfen and Redbank: bell-founders, marshland bowyers and orchard caravans. Crafted emblems and local histories replace the generic kingdom identities; their strengths and tradeoffs remain the same.

Workers chop, hoe, gather and build with distinct tool motions. Melee troops, archers, riders and siege engines wind up, strike and recover. Actions follow their existing gathering and combat timing, including online replicas.
Both online players must reload for the redesigned terrain. The Standard Sacred clock remains three minutes; the experimental scoring delay is not included.

releases.title: Little kingdoms, distinct character
releases.summary: A new miniature art style for every kingdom, with clearer match setup and a warmer menu.
changes: Choose your kingdom directly in New Game. Your crest and kingdom name are visible beside the match options, with a separate rival choice for solo games.

Every kingdom has six refreshed unit roles and ten building illustrations. Crownlands uses teal and limestone, Verdant uses green and oak, and Sunstride uses terracotta and bronze. Longbows and Outriders retain their signature roles.
Recruitment portraits, building cards and construction previews use the same new art as the battlefield. Ownership marks distinguish friendly and rival armies without recolouring their materials.
A shared miniature village illustration, cleaner headings, softer panels and a new castle icon replace older menu and welcome-page graphics.

Unit costs, civilization bonuses, combat timing, building footprints, victory rules and protocol 3 remain unchanged. The existing recovery controls remain available; the late idle-browser error is still under investigation.

releases.title: Steadier controls, easier building
releases.summary: Find room for buildings, keep recruitment controls steady and recover from browser errors.
changes: Find space suggests visible, clear ground for a building in your current view. Review the preview, then tap Place to pay and build. Fog messages explain when the whole footprint needs to move into sight.
Selected-building controls keep their intended positions after opening and closing panels, so recruitment buttons stay where you expect them.
After a browser error, a recovery notice offers Save log, Reload game and Dismiss. Reloading is your choice and leaves the current match.

releases.title: Hold your ground
releases.summary: Defend the Sacred Site with fighters, bring mixed armies together and build with steadier mobile controls.
changes: In Standard matches, keep at least one fighter in the Sacred Site ring to run its victory clock. Scouts and workers can still claim and contest it. Leaving pauses your progress; returning resumes it. Uncontested ownership still earns gold. Control race keeps its existing rules.

Nearby mixed fighters receiving a compatible Attack order march at a shared pace until combat. Move keeps each unit's normal speed for scouting and withdrawal. Selection shows when fighters are marching together. Both online players need this release.
Select fighters and Find army gather your armed troops without pulling Scouts away from their scouting routes.
Castle unlocks the Siege Workshop in 20-, 30- and 40-population matches. The Army build row scrolls on narrow screens so every building stays reachable.
Construction cards keep the same order as you advance through the ages, including House and Town Center.
The guided opener lets you advance when you can afford it. Assigning a worker to food counts toward its food lesson; you can end the guide and continue playing.
Rotating or resizing a paused game preserves your chosen camera zoom.
Economy makes idle workers easier to spot and assign. Army Info can explain repeated counter losses your troops actually witnessed.

releases.title: Three kingdoms
releases.summary: Choose your kingdom, recruit from the field and keep your village working.
changes: Choose Crownlands for a flexible army and full-strength defenses, Verdant League for a stronger wood economy and long-range Longbows, or Sunstride Clans for faster food harvesting and swift Outriders. Each specialty brings a real tradeoff.
Choose your solo rival's kingdom, or bring your own into an online lobby. Original crests and signature-unit artwork make each choice recognizable. Both online players need this release.

Army now includes Recruit alongside Groups. Train reinforcements without finding each military building. See the full paid queue, understand Repeat and rally choices, and switch pages without moving the shared controls.
A worker who finishes a Farm starts farming immediately and keeps any resources already carried. Economy warns when nearby visible food runs low and names a sustained food-work gap.
Solo matches pause when you leave the app, switch tabs or turn your phone upright. Resume when ready. Online matches keep running.
Results can explain repeated, witnessed counter-unit losses and suggest a better army mix, using your kingdom's troop names.
The opponent can invest in worker protection, hauling and a useful second Resource Camp when its economy can support them. Army choices consider its kingdom as well as enemies it has seen.
Tapping a visible building roof now selects the building more reliably, while nearby units and transparent space keep their existing selection rules.

releases.title: Read the battle
releases.summary: Distinct mounted troops, richer buildings and army information within a tap.
changes: Horsemen and siege engines gain clearer equipment, material contrast and team cloth. Siege carriages stay grounded as they move and recoil when firing.
Roof eaves, timber frames, stone foundations and building-specific details make your settlement easier to recognize. Construction rises from the ground behind temporary scaffolding.
Building hits use a brief warm pulse that preserves team and construction colors, including online play. Reduced flashes still suppresses it.
Mixed armies show readable unit counts. Tap selection Info for the full composition, combined health, roles and available attack, armor, range and stance details.
Attack poses follow the existing weapon release timing. Unit sizes, combat strength, costs and building footprints are unchanged.

releases.title: A living battlefield
releases.summary: Richer woods and water, clearer worker loads, and useful status at a glance.
changes: Original oak, elm and pine silhouettes, grounded fruit and mineral deposits, quieter meadows and deeper water bring the battlefield together.
Workers carry recognizable food, timber, ore and mixed-load symbols. Selected workers show how full their bag is.
Selection meters name health, stock, construction and capture progress. Local Farms show whether a worker is assigned, and population feedback explains reserved queue space.
Online foundations no longer show a missing-builder warning based on incomplete client information.
Reduced server work as armies grow, while preserving current vision and targeting rules.

releases.title: A clear path to your lobby
releases.summary: Join a friend opens with readable battlefield previews and reachable room controls.
changes: Opening multiplayer directly from Home now settles the game-creation layout after its text wraps.
The multiplayer, shared battlefield selection and interface improvements from beta.9 and beta.10 are included.

releases.title: Ready to start
releases.summary: New Game keeps Start and Leave room visible in browser windows and small landscape screens.
changes: The lobby and game-creation layout now account for browser controls, safe areas and margins before choosing the larger map cards.
On the shortest screens, battlefield details scroll while the map choices and match actions stay within reach.
The multiplayer stability, shared map selection and command-table redesign from beta.9 are included.

releases.title: Your battlefield. Your company.
releases.summary: Choose a battlefield in New Game, invite a friend to a private room, and command through a redesigned interface.
changes: New Game now contains the map previews, match rules and opponent options. Settings keeps audio, controls and display preferences.
Create a private multiplayer room and share its code. The host chooses Open Plains, River Crossings or Woodland Flanks; both players see the choice before starting.
A shared navy, parchment and gold interface brings clearer headings, labeled commands and readable construction, recruitment, research, pause and results panels.
Multiplayer handles loading delays and final results more reliably, and safely ignores input references to units removed by a newer snapshot.
Recent building clearance, Farm ownership, resource delivery, crowd movement and combat improvements are included. A lost connection still ends the current match; return to New Game to play again.

releases.title: Find your fighters
releases.summary: Small selection brackets help you keep track of your units in a crowded fight.
changes: Selected units gain small, hollow foot brackets that stay visible above overlapping fighters. The brackets keep the same size as you zoom.
The cue follows your Clear player markers setting and clears when you deselect a unit. It appears only for your living units in current vision.

releases.title: Hold the site
releases.summary: An early Sacred claim on Easy now gives you a reason to bring reinforcements.
changes: Easy can respond to your Sacred claim from 2:30 with its existing small, paid force. Scout the site, then bring troops to hold it.
Ordinary base raids still wait until 5:00, and Easy starts its own neutral-site initiative at 6:30. Its 45-second regroup after a field loss remains.
Training, costs, gathering and unit strength retain their existing rules. Medium and Hard keep their current response policy.
The large Sacred badge clears when its ground is visible, so it no longer covers the units fighting there. The capture ring and top status remain, and the badge returns when vision is lost.

releases.title: Read the ground
releases.summary: Clearer river banks, grounded resource colors and quieter management screens.
changes: Narrow bank and shallows details make river edges easier to read. The meadow has softer variation so units and useful terrain stand out.
Trees use moss tones, food grows in small fruit clusters, and gold appears in neutral rock with ochre facets. Gathering, stock and touch footprints retain their existing rules.
Ordinary notifications stay out of management and modal sheets. Current messages return when you close the sheet; expired messages stay retired. Raid cards keep their own reachable lane.
An actionable notification now responds once to a tap, including when the browser also sends an emulated mouse event.

releases.title: Fieldcraft
releases.summary: Army field notes, more responsive guards and original working yards.
changes: Open Army, then Info for three short field notes: assemble slower troops, attack-move together, and withdraw before your next push. Back returns to your groups without changing selection.
Stand Ground troops stop repeatedly choosing enemies beyond their reach and respond when an enemy enters range. Weapon reach, damage and direct orders retain their existing rules.
The Blacksmith has a limewashed chimney, ember hearth and iron anvil. The Siege Workshop has an open assembly floor, timber crane and carriage wheel. Both use the companyâ€™s teal and clay materials.

releases.title: Your company, in the field
releases.summary: Recognizable miniatures, purpose-built architecture and a clearer view of the battle.
changes: The Builder carries his shoulder mallet beneath a broad straw hat; the Warrior bears the company shield; the Archer brings her copper hair and open bow to the battlefield. Their existing roles and combat rules stay the same.
Resource Camps have open supply shelters, Archery Ranges have practice targets, and Stables have timber bays. Each has matching teal and clay team materials.
Opening guidance steps aside while you manage workers, troops or settings, then returns with the current instruction. Placement guidance remains available.
Raid alerts remain reachable beside Economy and Army. Tap an alert to close management and view the threatened location while keeping your selected units.

releases.title: Room to learn. Room to play.
releases.summary: A full-screen battlefield, a gentler Easy opponent and architecture made for the company.
changes: Menu backgrounds and battlefields fill the phone screen. Controls stay clear of camera cutouts and the home indicator, including when you rotate the phone.
Easy sends smaller squads, gives you longer to establish your village and regroups after losing a fighter. Medium and Hard retain their pressure.
The Town Center, House and Barracks have original silhouettes, mineral roofs, timber details and pale stone. Enemy roofs and banners use clay colours while their materials stay natural.
Browser controls share the custom command plates. Notices use clearer type and quieter colours; the problem-report form respects the phone safe area.

releases.title: A company worth commanding
releases.summary: An original cast, bespoke controls and three battlefields with room for different tactics.
changes: Meet the Builder, Warrior and Archer in a new character-led menu. Custom command plates, equipment-inspired icons and quieter battlefield markers give the game a consistent identity.
Choose Open Plains, River Crossings or Woodland Flanks in Settings â†’ Map. Save a seed to revisit a battlefield.
River maps have three broad crossings. Woodland maps offer attack lanes around deep forests. Both keep opening resources close and expansions reachable.
Online rivals receive the same map and seed. Updated players can meet on all three styles; matches with older clients retain Open Plains.
Melee fighters make room for allies while attacking, reducing stacks of units on a shared target.
The AI can rebalance its workers when another worker is unable to find a job, keeping paid military production moving.

releases.title: Find a rival. Build your kingdom.
releases.summary: Online 1v1, quicker openings and simpler touch controls.
changes: Choose Online 1v1 to search for another player. Matches run on a shared authoritative server; search can be cancelled and disconnects produce a clear result.
Tap ground to move without stopping for enemies. Hold ground to attack-move. Drag to pan, pinch to zoom, and use the area-selection icon before dragging around an army.
Build choices, worker management, training and settings fit compact pages without scrolling. Short, distinct markers show move, gather, attack and rally orders.
Farms provide food indefinitely. One Resource Camp accepts food, wood and gold; workers choose reachable drop-offs and preserve carried resources when reassigned.
Larger opening supplies, faster paid training and better delivery rates bring armies forward. Standard Sacred victory now requires three minutes of uninterrupted control.
Units keep movement intent under fire, defend nearby allies and limit autonomous pursuit. Production exits avoid isolated pockets beside buildings.

releases.title: A better fit for your phone
releases.summary: Cleaner shapes, less stacked interface and comfortable controls on smaller screens.
changes: Primary commands now use matching square buttons; extra orders open beside the management controls to leave more of the battlefield visible.
Build categories have compact tabs and consistently sized cards. Army fits its contents, while Economy adapts its worker controls to narrower screens.
Worker job counts live in Economy, removing a duplicate strip above the command dock. Names, prices, shortages and finite Farm food remain available where you make decisions.
Smaller screens automatically receive a minimum control-size adjustment. Your interface-size preference still applies on top.

releases.title: More battlefield. Fewer labels.
releases.summary: Compact icon controls open the actions you need, with names and costs where decisions happen.
changes: Reach Base, Economy and Army through compact icons with unit counts and economy alerts. Tap Economy or Army again to close its panel.
Move, attack, select an area and expand camera or extra orders from recognizable icons. Armed commands stay highlighted; Info and optional holds explain every action.
Recruit from unit portraits with clear names and full costs. Queue badges show pending units; Repeat keeps its ON/OFF state and any shortage visible.
See more building choices at once, with names, prices and requirements retained. Finite Farm food remains explicit.
Read food, wood, gold and population from distinct symbols and numerical counters. Larger maps, camera zoom and match rules are unchanged.

releases.title: Room to explore. Room to fight.
releases.summary: Larger battlefields, a wider camera view and more reasons to scout the flanks.
changes: Every population setting now plays on a 72 by 72 battlefield, with more than twice the previous area.
Discover two finite food, wood and gold expansion pockets on each side. Nearby opening resources remain balanced between rivals.
Zoom farther out for an overview. Wheel and button zoom ease around your focus; small trackpad movements make smaller adjustments. Pinch follows your fingers, and Reduced motion keeps zoom immediate.

Villagers work through each gathering cycle faster for both players, with wood gathering matching food to help fund buildings and reinforcements. Resources still need real delivery, Farms still run out, and every recruit and building still costs resources.
AI workers keep looking for new resources when a search route is blocked, so trapped workers cannot use up the whole team's exploration plan. The opponent still has to scout before finding resources.

Standard now needs four minutes of Sacred control. Contests pause your clock and losing ownership resets it. Control race keeps banking its four minutes across captures; destroying the enemy Town Center still wins either mode.

releases.title: Your kingdom, ready to go
releases.summary: A proper welcome in your browser. A direct route into the game from your Home Screen.
changes: Learn the game and find installation steps for iPhone, iPad, Android and desktop.
Play in your browser whenever you prefer. Installation is optional.
Online update checks happen automatically. Ready updates apply at the main menu, with active matches and their results protected.
Find these release notes from the welcome page, main menu or Pause screen.

releases.title: Keep your kingdom in the fight
releases.summary: Clearer economy decisions and a new optional way to contest the map.
changes: Economy now warns when worked food is running low and explains finite Farms: 75 wood buys a field containing 300 food.
See production shortages, counter roles and rally destinations without relying on tooltips.
Economy and Army stay open when a selected unit falls, so the next reinforcement order remains within reach.
Control race offers cheaper paid Feudal and military buildings. Bank four minutes of exclusive Sacred control; contests pause scoring. Standard rules remain available.
Report a problem directly from the result screen using the existing private report flow.

releases.title: Less menu work. More strategy.
releases.summary: Mobile management, deliberate gestures and persistent settings.
changes: Reach Base, Economy and Army quickly, save two groups, and manage paid production away from home.
Reassign workers, follow raid warnings and locate the Sacred site while keeping the battlefield visible.
Adjust interface size, camera and audio preferences. Settings stay on this device.
Web audio routing and background transitions have been improved.
